increment: Folded arXiv:2609.05279 (Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams; Gao et al.; 2026-09-04). Eight teams formed independently from one base model, agents keep private notebooks over 10 episodes, then role-matched agents traded between teams vs a placebo. FINDINGS: a swap costs little task score but raises communication-per-progress by 16-63%; in Hanabi a swapped agent is MORE expensive than an inexperienced one (convention interference from the former partner); in Collab-Overcooked when the agenda-setter is swapped, most extra communication comes from the agent that STAYED; the penalty tracks how far independently-formed teams drift apart. WHY IT LANDS: swarm_demo's fresh-eyes rule and the design's 'roles are transient' stance assume rotation is free - this prices it. The substrate's rotation buys AUDIT VALIDITY and the cost is COMMUNICATION OVERHEAD not correctness, so it is a measured tradeoff not a refutation: rotate for safety where safety needs it (the gates), let stable pairs persist elsewhere, and budget the STAYER's re-coordination cost when the personal-assistant role churns. Reframes emergent_social_conventions: a capability that is also a liability on transfer. +1 node, +7 edges.
